## What is LCOE?

The **levelized cost of energy** is the average price per unit of electricity
that pays back *all* lifetime costs of a plant.

$$
\text{LCOE} = \frac{\text{lifetime costs}}{\text{lifetime energy produced}}
$$

It lets us compare a solar farm, a gas plant, and a reactor on the **same
footing** — dollars per megawatt-hour.

## A simple calculation

A solar farm costs **\$1,000,000** to build, runs **25 years**, and makes
**2,500 MWh per year**.

$$
\text{LCOE} = \frac{\$1{,}000{,}000}{25 \times 2{,}500\ \text{MWh}} = \$16\,/\text{MWh}
$$

*(Real estimates add fuel, maintenance, and a discount rate — but the idea is
the same.)*

## Rough LCOE by source

| Source        | Typical LCOE ($/MWh) |
|---------------|:--------------------:|
| Utility solar |        30 – 40       |
| Onshore wind  |        25 – 50       |
| Natural gas   |        45 – 75       |
| Nuclear       |        55 – 90       |
| Coal          |        65 – 150      |

Cheapest on paper isn't the whole story — **land, waste, and human cost** don't
appear here.

## Takeaway

LCOE is a powerful *first* comparison —

but a fair energy choice weighs the costs it **leaves out**.
